[7] You'll be prepared to excel in a rewarding career with the leadership skills needed to create a thriving healthcare organization. ProgramName: Doctor of Chiropractic, D.C.
Requirements: Applicants to the Chiropractic Program at Campbellsville University must meet the following minimum requirements in order to be considered for admissions. Requirements are: 90 undergraduate credits from a regionally accredited institution. Of the 90 credits, 24 credits will come from life and/or physical sciences with half of these courses including a laboratory component. 3.0 GPA. [17] To be considered for acceptance into the School of Chiropractic, students must submit the following required documents: A completed Campbellsville University application to the Doctor of Chiropractic program; Official transcripts from all previously attended post-secondary institutions; Two letters of recommendation: one from a professor and one from a professional; A one-page personal statement describing your interest and intent to pursue our Doctor of Chiropractic degree. [16] An interview with a DCP faculty is also required. [17]
Description: The Doctor of Chiropractic Program at Campbellsville University is a rigorous, ten-trimester program of study. The curriculum is built upon the Campbellsville University mission and the chiropractic profession’s emphasis on the patient-practitioner relationship, evidence-based practice, and the body’s innate ability to self-heal and self-regulate. Students are trained as primary care providers to diagnose and treat a wide array of human ailments. Students learn a variety of chiropractic techniques, diagnostic procedures, and practice management skills. The program culminates with a one-year clinical internship where students will provide patient care under the direct supervision of a licensed doctor of chiropractic.
Accredidation: The Doctor of Chiropractic degree program at Campbellsville University is pursuing programmatic accreditation from the Council on Chiropractic Education (CCE). The program has been approved by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) and the Kentucky Council on Postsecondary Education (CPE).

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Education, M.A. Ed.
Requirements:
ADMISSION REQUIREMENTS

1. A completed Graduate Application for Admission.
2. A baccalaureate degree from an accredited college with a minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale.
3. A verbal and quantitative score on the Graduate Record Examination (GRE). A GRE score is not required if the student has a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. The GRE requirement is waived for all certification and Rank I programs in education, with the exception of the Master of Arts in School Improvement (Rank II/principalship) program and applicants who do not have at least a 2.75 GPA.
4. Three letters of recommendation from persons who can attest to the academic and/or professional capabilities of the applicant.
5. A written statement of purpose for entering the program and professional goals (300-500 words).
6. A valid teaching certificate (or statement of eligibility) for any certification program.
7. Additional requirements exist for some programs. Check the requirements under the specific program of interest.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Educational Administration (Principal P-12)
Description: The Master of Arts in Educational Administration (Principal P-12) program is designed to prepare educators for positions as elementary, middle, and high school principals.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP).

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Educational Administration (Superintendent)
Requirements: In order to apply to Campbellsville University's Master of Arts in Educational Administration online, future students must submit or complete the following: Complete the online application. All official college transcripts from each college or university previously and currently attended confirming a cumulative 3.0 GPA. Copy of valid teaching certificate. Leadership portfolio. Documentation of two years as a school/district administrator. CA-TP (for Option 6 Candidates). [2, 3, 4]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Educational Administration (Supervisor of Instruction)
Requirements: In order to apply to Campbellsville University's accredited online Master's in Educational Administration: Supervisor of Instruction P-12 program, prospective students must submit or complete the following: Complete the online application. All official college transcripts from each college or university previously and currently attended confirming a cumulative 3.0 GPA. Copy of valid teaching certificate – Rank II. [2, 3]
Description: The fully online Master's in Educational Administration (Supervisor of Instruction P-12) equips candidates with the tools to practice Christian servant leadership as district-level administrators. [3]  The central focus of the program is to prepare educational leaders to empower students by offering support to teachers of all levels. [3] Further, the program specifically caters to caring teachers who strive to positively impact student learning. [3] The program's curriculum has been structured with careful consideration by leaders in education. [3] Through a close relationship with surrounding P-12 partner districts, Campbellsville University has developed an advisory council to construct the online program. [3] The council consists of administrators who draw on their educational and personal experiences to give students in the M.A. in Educational Administration a skill set to lead in the field. [3] In as few as 18 months, candidates can complete the program. [3] From its focus on content, process and self-efficacy learning experiences, the program calls on candidates to view education as empowerment. [3] As students complete the program, they will have the opportunity to apply that ethos to the highest levels of leadership in education. [3]
Accredidation: Campbellsville's education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and are approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher education and certification. [3, 4, 5, 9] Campbellsville University is also accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC). [4, 9]

ProgramName: Education Specialist, Ed.S. in Educational Administration (Principal, Supervisor of Instruction and Director of Pupil Personnel)
Requirements: The Ed.S. in Educational Administration (Supervisor of Instruction, District Pupil Personnel, and Principal) will prepare candidates to practice Christian servant leadership in a variety of school and district level administrator positions in the P-12 school system. Educational Admin, Ed.S., (Principal, Supervisor of Instruction and DPP) requirement: 51 Hours. [10]
Concentration: ['School Principal', 'District Administration (Director of Pupil Personnel/Supervisor of Instruction)']
Description: The Education Specialist (Ed. S.) program offers advanced preparation for leadership roles, including principal, supervisor of instruction, and director of pupil personnel. This program deepens skills in organizational leadership, staff development, and student services within a Christ-centered educational philosophy. [5] The specific goal is to provide the preparation needed for certification for School Principal Levels I and II, Supervisor of Instruction Levels I and II, Director of Pupil Personnel Levels I and II, or Superintendent of Schools. [2] The 30-hour minimum requirement is a structured program oriented toward the candidate's professional objectives. [2]
Accredidation: Campbellsville University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC). Additionally, Campbellsville's education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and are approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher education and certification. [4, 6]

ProgramName: Education Specialist, Ed.S. in Educational Administration (Supervisor of Instruction, DPP, Superintendent)
Requirements:
1. Official transcripts of all colleges attended.
2. Master's Degree (Rank II) from an accredited institution.
3. Recommendation from school superintendent.
4. Valid teaching certificate.
Description: The Education Specialist (Ed.S.) in Educational Administration is an online program that prepares candidates for all three (3) of the following leadership roles: Supervisor of Instruction, Director of Pupil Personnel (DPP), and Superintendent. The program is designed for candidates who hold a master’s degree and a Rank II certification. The curriculum focuses on developing advanced skills in educational leadership, strategic planning, and instructional supervision. Candidates will engage in coursework that covers topics such as school law, finance, human resources, and curriculum development from a district-level perspective. The program includes practical experiences, allowing students to apply their knowledge in real-world settings.
Accredidation: The Education Specialist (Ed.S.) degree program has been approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB). Campbellsville University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC). [3] Additionally, Campbellsville's education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP). [3]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in School Counseling, M.A.S.C.
Description: Campbellsville University's School Counseling (M.A.S.C.) program prepares students to become effective counselors in K-12 educational settings. This program combines comprehensive coursework in counseling theory, ethical practices, and school systems with hands-on experience in providing guidance and support to students. Graduates are equipped to address the social, emotional, and academic needs of students, promoting their overall well-being and success. The M.A.S.C. program is designed to help future school counselors create a positive, supportive environment for students across all grade levels.
Accredidation: Campbellsville University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC). Campbellsville's education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and are approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher education and certification.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Special Education/Initial Certification, M.A.S.E.
Requirements: Admission to the M.A.S.E. program is a two-part process that requires admission to the Teacher Education Program and the Graduate School. Candidates must meet the admission requirements for both to be fully admitted to the program. Requirements for admission to the Teacher Education Program can be found in the Teacher Education Handbook available in the School of Education or online.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching (IECE/Initial Certificate)
Requirements: The MAT program is designed for candidates able to be hired in Kentucky as an option 6 candidate or student teach in the state of Kentucky. CAP 5 is admission to the program where candidates must have a cumulative GPA of 2.75 as documented on official transcript for a Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (or 3.0 on last 30 hours). Further candidates must provide Three (3) Disposition recommendations (recommended: immediate supervisor, colleague, self), a clear criminal background check, and self-assessment of dispositions and Pre-Professional Goals Assessment. They must also sign and commit to the KY Code of Ethics, the National Association for the Education of Young Children Code of Ethics, the Council for Exceptional Children - Division of Early Childhood Code of Ethics, and the First Steps Provider Code of Ethical Conduct, entrees a diversity survey, and a creativity self-assessment, and sign the unit's disposition assessment policy. Candidates must successfully complete an entrance interview at which time a presentation is made by the candidate which is scored using a rubric that includes assessment of the 4 Cs 21st Century Skills (creativity, collaboration, communication, and critical thinking). Lastly, upon admission, candidates must provide a Praxis II Study Plan/Statement of Understanding. [3]
Description: The Master of Arts in Teaching (M.A.T.) with a concentration in Interdisciplinary Early Childhood Education (IECE) is a program for those persons who hold a bachelor’s degree in a field other than teacher education and who wish to become certified to teach young children from birth to kindergarten in the Commonwealth of Kentucky. It is also for those persons who may already hold teacher certification in another area and who wish to add certification in IECE. The program has been approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher certification. Campbellsville University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC) to award associate, baccalaureate, and masters degrees. The Campbellsville University teacher education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and are approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher certification and rank change.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching (Middle Grades 5-9/Initial Certificate)
Term: The university operates on a semester system with Fall and Spring semesters. [4] Online programs offer six start dates throughout the year. [2]
Description: The online master's of teaching middle grades from Campbellsville University was designed for those who wish to transition into a teaching career and already have a bachelor's degree in a relevant field. [3] The program provides you with the skills needed to work with diverse learners, apply effective teaching methods and understand relevant topics in student growth and development. [3] You will receive the certification required to teach your chosen subject while learning the modern trends that are evolving education. [3] The program teaches the cognitive, physical and social-emotional growth of children and adolescents; a variety of instructional approaches, materials and comprehensive curriculum to support student learning in literacy; and the practical skills in student assessment required for curriculum planning in the classroom. [3] The online M.A.T. degree also covers the research methods and procedures used in education, effective management skills and the needs and nature of diverse populations. [3]

[3]

Candidates will acquire the knowledge, skills, and dispositions to be effective teachers. ProgramName: Master of Arts in Teaching (Grades 8-12/Initial Certificate)
Description: Campbellsville University's MAT program (8-12) is both a traditional (36 hours) and Option 6 alternative certification (30 hours) program uniquely designed to reflect a professional learning community. It will be delivered by education and Arts and Science faulty [sic] faculty] in collaboration and partnership with area school district personnel. Candidates will acquire the knowledge, skills, and dispositions to be effective teachers. The outcome will be documented in several critical assessments - the electronic portfolio and during field and clinical experiences. Mentoring for alternative certification candidates is consistently and intentionally planned for the duration of the candidate's employment on the temporary provisional certificate. Courses will be taught in an online, each designed in eight-week graduate terms. The secondary grades certification MAT program consists of education and special teaching methods coursework, as well as an action research project proposal and a semester long student-teaching experience for traditional candidates. Content literacy program requirements for reading and writing (16 KAR 5:060) are addressed specifically in the ED 659 course and are required to be included in all instruction. The professor for ED 659 has a terminal degree in reading. Option 6 alternative route candidates will have a mentor while functioning in their own classroom setting. [5]

ProgramName: Master of Education in Montessori Education, M. Ed.
Description: The selection revitalizationof revitalizationcourses and the content included were developed with the goal revitalizationof revitalizationpreparing graduates with the ability to provide positive influence as master teachers, directors, administrators, specialists, and higher education instructors individually and in collaboration with others. The coursework includes a professional education core of 9-15 credits designed to broaden candidate's knowledge of research, current trends in early childhood, and best practices in inclusive education. The Montessori Core consists of 21 credits of Montessori philosophy, curriculum and methods, observation, classroom management, and leadership coursework. An additional 6 credits is earned in a Montessori practicum. Upon completion of all course and practicum requirements, candidates receive a Montessori teacher certificate that is recognized worldwide, for the early childhood level ages two-and-a-half through six years.
Accredidation: The curriculum content was aligned with the Montessori Accreditation Council for Teacher Education (MACTE), the American Montessori Society (AMS), the Interstate Teacher Assessment and Support Consortium (InTASC), and the National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC) standards for the preparation of advanced early childhood professionals.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Applied Behavior Analysis, M.S.A.B.A.
Requirements: To enroll in a graduate program at Campbellsville University, the first step is to apply. An enrollment counselor will work with you to gather the necessary documentation that the school/college will use to determine your eligibility and potential admission. All candidates must submit a graduate application and official transcripts from the institution granting the bachelor's degree and any subsequent degrees or coursework. [4]

Description: The aaster of cience in pplied ehavior nalysis utilizes both learning and behavior theory in preparing candidates to work with clients who exhibit problem behaviors. andidates learn to implement behavior assessment tools and techniques, to analyze the data generated by the assessments, and to develop intervention plans for helping clients eliminate problem behaviors. pplied ehavior nalysis is useful for working with clients who have utism pectrum isorder, anger management issues, anxiety disorders, impulse control issues, behavioral addictions, , and many other life impacting conditions. ProgramName: Master of Science with Moderate Severe Disabilities, M.S.D.
Requirements: A student may enter the Master of Science with Moderate/Severe Disabilities with a bachelor’s degree and a minimum G.P.A. of 2.5, or a G.P.A. of 3.0 in the last thirty hours of credit completed, on the undergraduate degree. The student must pass the general education content courses of the appropriate age group of the certification they seek before student teaching. These courses include English, math, science, and social studies. Students who have a teaching degree are exempt from this requirement.
Description: The Moderate and Severe Disabilities, P-12 Program is a twenty-one (21) hour program designed to give candidates the opportunity to acquire knowledge, gain skills in identifying and assessing the needs of students, planning instruction and assessments for students with moderate and severe disabilities and with autism spectrum disorders. [2] Three options for MSD certification are available to candidates; (1) certification only, (2) as a certification component to the Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Special Education and (3) as a specialty option to Rank I/Master of Arts in School Improvement. [2] Major assessments include a student centered Individual Education Plan (IEP) based on assessment data administered and analyzed by the candidate, and a Behavior Intervention Plan. [2] Two additional assessments required for candidates pursuing MSD certification include the Master's Action Research Project (MARP) for TLMASE candidates, and the culminating project for MASI candidates. [2]
Accredidation: All School of Education programs leading to certification or rank change are approved by the Education Professional Standards Board (EPSB). Teacher education and certification programs are accredited by the Council for Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) as of May 2020. [5]

ProgramName: Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Education, T.L.M.A.E.
Concentration: ['Interdisciplinary Early Childhood Education', 'Special Education (LBD)', 'English as a Second Language', 'Gifted and Talented', 'Environmental Education']
Description: The Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Education (T.L.M.A.E.) is a 30-credit hour, field-based program designed to develop the knowledge, skills, and dispositions of a Teacher Leader. The Teacher Leader Model Standards (2011) and the Kentucky Teacher Standards (2011) serve as the foundation for the program. Each standard is addressed in the context of seven domains: a) fostering a collaborative culture to support educator development and student learning, b) accessing and using research to improve practice and student learning, c) promoting professional learning for continuous improvement, d) facilitating improvements in instruction and student learning, e) promoting the use of assessments and data for school and district improvement, f) improving outreach and collaboration with families and community, and g) advocating for student learning and the profession. Candidates successfully completing the degree requirements will be recommended for a change in rank and the Teacher Leader Endorsement. Candidates who have an undergraduate degree in a field other than education may earn the Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Education if they hold an alternative teaching certificate. A T&L area of concentration is also available through the School of Education. Five areas of concentration are available through the T&L M.A.E. program: Interdisciplinary Early Childhood Education, Special Education (LBD), English as a Second Language, Gifted and Talented, and Environmental Education. Each concentration area is comprised of twelve credit hours. Candidates must pass the appropriate PRAXIS specialty area exam for each area of concentration for which they are seeking certification. The Director of Graduate Programs in the School of Education should be consulted regarding concentration coursework and practicum requirements.
Accredidation: The Teacher Education Program at Campbellsville University is accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and is approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) to offer teacher education programs.

ProgramName: Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Special Education, T.L.M.A.S.E.
Description: The Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Special Education Program is a traditional certification program for graduate candidates who want to teach students who have learning and behavior disabilities in grades P-12. [1] It is a 30-hour, cohort model program. [5] Upon acceptance into the program, candidates will enroll in a cluster of professional proficiency courses totaling 15 hours. [5] The remaining 15 hours in the program, professional education courses, will be courses in the Teacher Leader Master of Arts in Education program. [5]

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate in Director of Special Education (Level I)
Requirements: Admission requirements for the Director of Special Education Level I program include: the online application, all official college transcripts confirming a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 or a 3.0 on the last 30 hours, a Master's degree or planned fifth-year program, a copy of your teaching certificate, and three years of experience as a special education teacher (or one year as a special education teacher and two as a school psychologist). [3, 9] Applicants must also provide the name and email address for a colleague and a building/district administrator for School of Education requirements and submit a complete statement of purpose. [3, 9]
Description: Focused on leadership in special education, the Graduate Certificate in Director of Special Education (Level I) equips professionals with the skills needed to oversee programs, support compliance, and advocate for students with exceptional needs. [2] This certificate is ideal for educators ready to take on administrative roles in special education settings. [2] The Level I certificate introduces foundational knowledge in special education leadership, law, policy, and service delivery systems. [3] Both levels emphasize ethical leadership, legal compliance, and student-focused program development, preparing graduates for influential roles in school and district-level special education administration. [3]
Accredidation: Campbellsville University's education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and are approved by the Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher education and certification. ProgramName: Graduate Certificate of School Counseling
Description: The graduate certificate in school counseling is for students who have a master’s degree in a related field but would like to become certified as a school counselor. The certificate is a 30-hour, non-degree program with an embedded 600-hour internship experience. Upon completion of the program, students can apply for school counseling certification.

ProgramName: Graduate Certificate of Superintendent
Requirements: To apply to Campbellsville University's superintendent certification online, future students must submit or complete the following: Complete the online application. All official college transcripts from each college or university previously and currently attended, confirming a cumulative 3.0 GPA. Copy of a valid teaching certificate. Master's degree. Leadership portfolio. Documentation of two years as a school/district administrator. CA-TP (for Option 6 Candidates). [2, 3]
Description: Campbellsville University's Graduate Certificate of Superintendent is designed for experienced educators seeking to advance into leadership roles at the district level. This program provides comprehensive training in educational leadership, policy, school finance, and district management, preparing graduates to lead and improve educational systems. Students will gain the skills necessary to make data-driven decisions, manage school operations, and effectively advocate for students and staff. The Superintendent certificate equips educators with the expertise to drive change and success across entire school districts, making a lasting impact on the education community.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music, M.A.M.
Master of Arts in Music: Musicology
Description: Campbellsville University's Master of Arts in Music (M.A.M.) is a flexible, academically rigorous program that prepares students for careers in music research, worship leadership, and church music ministry. [3] With concentrations in Musicology and Worship, the program is ideal for musicians who want to deepen their knowledge of music's meaning, history, and role in faith communities. [3] Designed for both full-time students and working professionals, the M.A.M. supports artistic development and critical thinking in a Christ-centered environment. [3] In the Musicology concentration, students engage in scholarly study of music history, literature, and analysis. [3] This concentration prepares students for roles in teaching, academic research, or further graduate study (e.g., Ph.D.). [3] You'll explore music's historical and cultural impact while developing advanced research and writing skills. [3]
Accredidation: The Campbellsville University School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [5]

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music: Worship
Requirements: Admission to the Music Graduate Program requires a bachelor's degree in music, or permission from the Graduate Music Admissions Committee. Applicants must submit two letters of recommendation, with one from an individual who can speak to the applicant's academic and/or professional capabilities or potential. Official transcripts of all college work from accredited institutions are required, confirming a minimum GPA of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale. For the Master of Arts in Music with a worship concentration, a Bachelor's Degree in Music or a related field from an accredited institution is necessary.
Description: The Master of Arts in Music degree is designed to provide the advanced study of music for students who have completed a baccalaureate degree in music. The program offers advanced studies in the areas of music education, church music, and performance. The purpose of the Master of Arts in Music is to provide a course of study that will enable the musician to develop professionally in a chosen field of emphasis and to provide a basis for doctoral study. The Master of Arts in Music degree is the non-thesis master’s degree in music. Upon completion of the Master of Arts in Music degree with an emphasis in Worship, the student will be able to: 1. Demonstrate advanced competencies as a worship leader. 2. Articulate a biblically-based philosophy of worship. 3. Exhibit administrative skills necessary to build a comprehensive worship ministry for the local church. 4. Apply learned theories and skills in a practical worship-leadership setting (practicum/internship).
Accredidation: Campbellsville University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges to award certificates, associate, baccalaureate, masters, and doctoral degrees. The School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Master of Music, M.M.
Description: The Master of Music degree is designed to provide the advanced professional competence and scholarship that is essential for a career in music. The degree program is built upon the framework of the Bachelor of Music degree and the Bachelor of Arts in Music degree and leads to a Master of Music degree in Music Education, Church Music, Performance, Conducting, Composition, or Piano Pedagogy. The major in Performance includes concentrations in voice, piano, organ, and orchestral instruments. The major in Conducting includes concentrations in the choral and instrumental areas.
Accredidation: The Campbellsville University School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Master of Music in Music Education, M.M.M.E.
Requirements:
Admission to the Master of Music in Music Education program requires the following:

1. Completed application for graduate admission.
2. A one-page, single-spaced statement of purpose articulating the applicant’s professional goals and objectives for graduate study.
3. Official transcripts from all colleges/universities attended sent directly to the Office of Graduate Admissions.
4. Three letters of recommendation. At least two of these should be from music professionals who can speak to the applicant’s potential for success as a graduate student and music educator.
5. A professional resume.
6. A scholarly writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to research and write at the graduate level.
7. A successful background check.
8. Evidence of a minimum undergraduate GPA of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale.
9. An appropriate bachelor’s degree in music education, or its equivalent, from an accredited institution. Applicants who do not hold a degree in music education will be considered on a case-by-case basis and may be required to complete leveling courses as determined by the Dean of the School of Music.
10. Interview with the Dean of the School of Music or the Graduate Music Coordinator.
Description: The Master of Music in Music Education degree is primarily intended for certified music educator having a Rank III teaching certificate, who are required, if teaching in the State of Kentucky, to attain the Master's level (Rank II) certification. [7] The degree can also assist non-certified musicians who have a bachelor's degree to prepare for further studies in doctoral programs and college-level teaching. [7] This degree does not certify individuals for public school teaching in the elementary or secondary schools unless Rank II certification was previously earned. [7]
Accredidation: Campbellsville University is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). [7]

ProgramName: Master of Music: Conducting
Description: The Master of Music program includes majors in performance, conducting, church music, composition, and music education. The purpose of the Master of Music degree is to provide for the development of professional competence in a major field and to develop advanced scholarly awareness and competence. All graduate programs in the School of Music are designed to give students a functional knowledge of the history and theory of music, and to provide them with the basic techniques for scholarly study and research.
Accredidation: The School of Music is accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Master of Music: Instrumental Performance
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Music program requires a bachelor's degree in music from an accredited institution. Applicants must have an undergraduate GPA of at least 2.5, or a 3.0 in their music major. If the GPA is below 2.5, a GRE score is required. Two letters of recommendation are also necessary. A statement of purpose that discusses the applicant's interest in and commitment to graduate study is also required. Additionally, all applicants must pass an entrance examination in music theory and music history and literature. An audition is also a key component of the application. International students must submit English proficiency test scores.
Description: To be considered for admission to the MM in Instrumental Performance, applicants must meet the following minimum requirements: 1. Hold a Bachelor’s degree in music from an accredited institution. 2. Have a cumulative grade point average of 3.0 in all previous collegiate work. 3. Score an 85 or higher on the TOEFL iBT of 6.5 or higher on the IELTS (international applicants only). Complete the following steps to apply to the MM: 1. Submit the online Graduate Admissions application. As part of this application MM applicants need to upload: a. Transcripts of course work from all schools attended. b. The purpose of the degree program is to provide graduate theological education that is Christ-centered, biblically-based, and ministry-focused. The curriculum is designed to equip students with the biblical and theological foundations for ministry, along with the practical skills to serve effectively in the local church and other ministry settings. Upon completion of the Master of Divinity degree program, graduates will be able to: interpret and apply the biblical text in a faithful and relevant manner; articulate a coherent and biblically-grounded theology; demonstrate the skills necessary for effective pastoral ministry, including preaching, teaching, counseling, and leadership; and integrate their faith and practice in a way that reflects a deep commitment to Christ and His kingdom. Students are encouraged to cultivate a vibrant devotional life, engage in meaningful relationships with faculty and peers, and participate in practical ministry experiences that will prepare them for a lifetime of service. Description: The Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts in Elementary Education, P-5 Certification program at Campbellsville University prepares future teachers for leading in early learning environments and elementary classrooms. [5] The curriculum is designed to equip students to teach all subjects at the elementary level, based on an interdisciplinary model that provides content knowledge in all core disciplines and the fine arts. [2] Students will gain practical skills in lesson planning, assessment, classroom management, and child development, grounded in a Christ-centered approach to teaching. [5] The program also covers instructional technology and strategies for working with diverse learners. [3] A significant component of the program is hands-on field experience, culminating in 16 weeks of student teaching in elementary classrooms to apply learned skills. [3, 5] Upon completion, graduates are prepared for Praxis® exams and are eligible to apply for initial teacher certification in Kentucky for primary through fifth-grade levels. [3, 5] The program is offered at the Campbellsville, Harrodsburg, Louisville, Somerset, and Elizabethtown campuses, as well as online. [2, 5]
Accredidation: Campbellsville University's education programs are accredited by the Council for the Accreditation of Educator Preparation (CAEP) and are approved by the state's Education Professional Standards Board of Kentucky (EPSB) for teacher education and certification. [3, 6]

[5] The Pharmacy Science Area is to be used in conjunction with either the agreement with the pharmacy program at Sullivan University or with the pharmacy program at the University of Kentucky. [2] The Sullivan University agreement is a 3+3 Accelerated Program in Pharmacy. Students will complete all of the necessary coursework at CU to enter the Doctor of Pharmacy program at Sullivan University in 3 years.
